focus: Process errors (c) to (e) and the generated-artifact drift family (f), plus the changelog version collision (g)
noveltyJustification: Six new findings: the scratch namespace-collision mechanism behind (c), the committed regenerations behind (d), the unverifiable-process-step mechanism behind (e), the designed source/generated split behind (f), the retrieval-fixtures family, and the branch-local version mint behind (g).

ruledOut: A version-reservation service or lock on changelog numbers - the collision is rare, both sides can read origin/main, and a reservation layer adds a dependency with no caller today
A scratch-lifecycle manager for packets - the convention exists; the missing piece is naming, not machinery

label: Process error (c) is a scratch namespace collision: disposable run outputs and planner helpers share one scratch directory, so a wildcard cleanup cannot tell them apart. Executors refuse rm -rf where configured (the round-one cli-codex run stopped because the command runner refuses it) and every later build brief carries explicit do-not-delete rules, but the incident itself is unrecorded; smallest fix is a tools/ child plus a cleanup rule pointed at run outputs only.

Process error (d) matches an observable artifact: the packet commits scratch as evidence, and one commit added three generations of the same unit tree (units/ 195 files, units-extra/ 32, units-extra2/ 8) with their generator scripts, so a regenerated tree is committed like any other output and nothing marks the authoritative generation; the incident record is absent and the introducing commit would settle it.

Process error (e) has a precise mechanism: tasks encode process steps whose only evidence is the executor's report, and the orchestrator's rerun rule (E2) can only recheck outcome criteria. Four recorded instances: skipped Phase 1 with no before files, before state not captured by the builder, builder captured no before-state files, and Task T009 with no build report for the contracts read; smallest fix is marking process-only tasks and requiring one artifact per process claim.

Process error (f) is a design decision with a cost: builders never run the Hermes generator or a compiled-route re-mint in write mode (round-four D4) because parallel children share the generated tree; every child therefore logs a PENDING-ORCHESTRATOR block (Hermes DRIFT sk-code/sk-code-review; compiled-route sk-code stale-manifest, Re-mint: sk-code) and the orchestrator clears each after the builds. An external user must know the writer commands; the gates name the drift but not the recovery.

The drift family is larger than the brief names: writers are sync-skills-hermes.cjs, the Codex and Pi agent syncs, compiled-route-manifest.cjs refresh plus its authored archive copy, generate-leaf-manifest.cjs and the trigger-index rebuild; the merge added a fifth family, the trigger index's retrieval fixtures (Rebuild the Hermes copy, the trigger index and its retrieval fixtures). The leaf-manifest defect was real and fixed: the walk listed git-ignored files so a Python test run made a committed manifest look stale.

Process error (g) is a branch-local version mint with no remote check: main minted system-spec-kit v2.7.1.0 for repairs and upgrades while the epic branch minted its own v2.7.1.0 for the hook stdin deadline; the merge kept main's and folded the branch's notes into v2.7.2.0. The version is minted from the local changelog folder so two branches forked before the other's mint both pick the same number; smallest fix is a changelog contract rule plus an origin/main read before minting.
